C: › [ C ] UK offensive something or someone considered unpleasant or difficult
討厭的事物（或人）；難辦的事

S or C: › [ S or C ] a rectangular piece that has been cut from an area of grass

example: Apparently he's a sod to work for.
據說爲他工作很麻煩。
What did you do that for, you stupid sod?
爲甚麽要那樣做，你這愚蠢的討厭鬼？
It was a sod of a car to repair.
這輛車很難修理。
He's won again - the lucky sod!
他又贏了——這小子真走運！
The poor old sod - I don't suppose he's got a home.
這可憐的老頭子——我覺得他沒有家。
He worked fast, cutting and slicing the turf neatly, heaving the sod to one side.
他做得很快，把草皮一塊塊整整齊齊地切割開來並拖到一邊。
She sleeps beneath the sod (= she is dead and has been buried).
她長眠九泉了。
Oh sod it - I've left my glasses behind!
哦，該死——我忘記拿眼鏡了！
Ann's just been chatting on the phone all morning - she's done sod all.
安整個上午都在打電話聊天——她什麽都沒做。
Oh sod off, you stupid git!
哦，滾開，你這白癡！
She told him to sod off.
她叫他滾開。

C: › [ C ] US also soda pop any type of sweet fizzy drink (= with bubbles) that is not alcoholic
C or U: › [ C or U ] also soda water, US also club soda a type of fizzy water (= with bubbles), often mixed with alcoholic drinks

NONE: › a bottle for filling water with gas and forcing it out under pressure to use in drinks
› (of something that can absorb water) extremely wet

example: The football field was absolutely sodden.
足球場完全是濕的。
Her thin coat quickly became sodden.
她的薄外套很快就濕透了。
Stupid sodding thing, why won't it move?
這該死的白癡，爲甚麽連動都不動？

› a white powder used to make foods rise when they are baked
› a chemical compound used as a water softener and in foods and industry, in the form of white powder or crystals
› a chemical compound used in soap and paper production and in powerful cleaning substances

caustic soda
